hindi: माना कि $A$ एक $3\times3$ वास्तविक आव्यूह है जिसके लिए $\mathrm{tr}(A)=6$, $\mathrm{tr}\left(A^{2}\right)=14$ तथा $\det(A)=6$ है, जहाँ $\mathrm{tr}(X)$ वर्ग आव्यूह $X$ का अनुरेख (trace) है। यदि किन्हीं वास्तविक संख्याओं $\beta$ तथा $\gamma$ के लिए $\mathrm{adj}(A)=A^{2}+\beta A+\gamma I$ है, जहाँ $I$, $3\times3$ तत्समक आव्यूह है, तो $(\beta,\gamma)$ बराबर है
solution: $\sum\lambda_i\lambda_j=\dfrac{36-14}{2}=11$, so the characteristic equation is $\lambda^{3}-6\lambda^{2}+11\lambda-6=0$, roots $1,2,3$
The eigenvalues are distinct, so no polynomial of degree $\le2$ kills $A$; hence $I,A,A^{2}$ are independent and $(\beta,\gamma)=(-6,11)$ is unique
solution_full: Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$ be the eigenvalues of $A$ (roots of $\det(A-\lambda I)=0$). Then $\mathrm{tr}(A)=\sum\lambda_i=6$, $\mathrm{tr}(A^{2})=\sum\lambda_i^{2}=14$ and $\det(A)=\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3=6$.
So the characteristic equation is $\lambda^{3}-6\lambda^{2}+11\lambda-6=0$, i.e. $(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)(\lambda-3)=0$; the eigenvalues are $1,2,3$.

Uniqueness: if $A^{2}+\beta A+\gamma I=A^{2}+\beta' A+\gamma' I$ with $(\beta,\gamma)\neq(\beta',\gamma')$, then $A$ would satisfy a non-zero polynomial of degree at most $1$, so $A$ would have at most one eigenvalue; but $A$ has three distinct eigenvalues. Hence $\beta=-6$, $\gamma=11$.
(Taking $\sum\lambda_i\lambda_j=14$ or a wrong sign gives the other options.)
originality_note: New: the characteristic polynomial is not given; it is rebuilt from tr A, tr A^2 and det A (power sums to elementary sums), and the adjugate is then read from Cayley-Hamilton (way 5). Closest known: 'if A^3 - ... = 0 find A^{-1} in terms of A' with an explicit matrix. Different because: no entries are given, the middle coefficient must be found from tr(A^2), and uniqueness of (beta, gamma) needs distinct eigenvalues.

concept_use.Characteristic Equation, Eigenvalues, &: tr A, tr A^2 and det A give the characteristic equation lambda^3 - 6 lambda^2 + 11 lambda - 6 = 0, and Cayley-Hamilton gives A^3 - 6A^2 + 11A - 6I = O.
concept_use.Adjoint of a square matrix: A adj(A) = det(A) I turns the Cayley-Hamilton identity into adj(A) = A^2 - 6A + 11I.

key_step: Getting the sum of pairwise eigenvalue products 11 from tr(A^2), then adj(A) = A^2 - 6A + 11I from Cayley-Hamilton.
justification: A routine chain of three standard results (power sums, Cayley-Hamilton, A adj A = det A I) with no hidden idea; options remove the risk. Similar demand to the determinant/trace statement checks of 2021-P1-Q11 (L2).
